name: Tommy Tuberville
quote: China is on the move and would love nothing more than to make American innovation a thing of the past… This bill gives us the upper hand over China by investing in research and development projects based in the United States.
sourceLabel: American Innovation and Jobs Act press release
notes: Also urged withdrawal of Biden AI Diffusion Rule as overly restrictive and harmful to U.S. competitiveness vs. China.

name: Ted Budd
quote: I firmly believe that our country's free-market, private sector-led way of doing things will be key to remaining ahead of Chinese state-backed AI developers… Congress can partner with the administration and industry to remove roadblocks and provide regulatory certainty to let innovators innovate.
sourceLabel: Senate Commerce subcommittee: America's AI Action Plan hearing

name: Christopher A. Coons
quote: The United States' prosperity and safety rests on our ability to win the AI race… This bipartisan resolution sets America on a path to win the AI race — one in which AI is built in the United States and our nation is stronger and safer.
sourceLabel: AI dominance resolution (with Cotton); also leads NO FAKES Act

name: Bill Cassidy
quote: Cosponsored the NO FAKES Act to establish federal protections against unauthorized AI-generated digital replicas of individuals' voice and likeness.

name: Richard J. Durbin

sourceLabel: DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (S. 1837)

name: Cory A. Booker
quote: Cosponsored the TAKE IT DOWN Act and Algorithmic Accountability Act to address non-consensual deepfakes and automated decision-system harms.
sourceLabel: TAKE IT DOWN Act (S. 146)

name: John Barrasso
quote: Cosponsored the TAKE IT DOWN Act to criminalize publication of non-consensual intimate images, including AI-generated deepfakes, without consent.
sourceLabel: TAKE IT DOWN Act (S. 146)

name: Adam B. Schiff
quote: Cosponsored the NO FAKES Act to protect individuals from unauthorized AI-generated replicas of their voice and likeness.
sourceLabel: NO FAKES Act of 2025 (S. 1367)

name: James Lankford
quote: Cosponsored the NO FAKES Act to establish federal protections against unauthorized AI-generated digital replicas.
sourceLabel: NO FAKES Act of 2025 (S. 1367)

name: Peter Welch
quote: Cosponsored the NO FAKES Act to protect Americans from unauthorized AI-generated replicas of voice and likeness.
sourceLabel: NO FAKES Act of 2025 (S. 1367)

name: Jack Reed
quote: Artificial intelligence models are being adopted at a rapid pace. While AI has massive potential to benefit society, we must recognize AI's security threats and ethical issues to ensure it's adopted in a manner that recognizes and mitigates these risks. This bipartisan framework addresses key catastrophic challenges posed by AI and the security protocols needed to safeguard against them.
sourceLabel: Romney-Reed-Moran-King extreme AI risks framework

name: Darline Graham
quote: I don't think these data centers should be built in people's backyards without community involvement and guardrails and regulations in place.
sourceLabel: WYFF4 interview on AI data centers

name: Tim Scott
quote: Fear and trepidation around electricity prices, water utilization, and aesthetics will stop the AI revolution from happening in America first, and it will empower China to beat America on this front if we don't get it right.
sourceLabel: South Carolina Business Council remarks on winning the AI race

name: Bill Hagerty
quote: The last thing I want to see is regulation that would shut down the innovation that AI promises. We need to win in this game. The United States needs to lead in this innovation.
sourceLabel: Fox Business interview on AI and financial system risks

name: John Cornyn
quote: Modern predators are exploiting advances in AI to develop new AI-generated child sexual abuse material, and technology companies are often unwittingly giving them the tools to do so.
sourceLabel: PROACTIV AI Data Act introduction

name: Tim Kaine
quote: There are valid concerns about A.I.'s potential negative uses—such as the errors it makes, its potential for spreading disinformation, or even whether its capabilities could be used to replace, rather than just supplement, human labor. Given those challenges and the fact that China is trying to replace America as the global leader in A.I., we need to stay one step ahead in the development and management of this technology.
sourceLabel: WSET interview on proactive AI governance

name: Patty Murray
quote: I want America to develop and deploy this technology. But, I want it to be transparent. I want it to be safe. And, I want to make sure that the benefits of AI are there for everyone.
sourceLabel: Seattle AI policy roundtable press release

name: Jeff Merkley
quote: In the face of bad actors abusing AI to spread disinformation about voting to further dangerous voter suppression efforts, the FAIR Elections Act will help take on this 21st-century threat and stand up to the Trump Administration's anti-democratic efforts to target eligible voters they don't like.
sourceLabel: FAIR Elections Act reintroduction press release

name: Peter Welch
quote: This is simple: if your work is used to train AI, there should be a way for you, the copyright holder, to determine that it's been used by a training model, and you should get compensated if it was.
sourceLabel: TRAIN Act reintroduction press release

name: John Barrasso
quote: Bad actors, like Russia and China, are given the green light to influence policy and keep us from producing American energy. This bill will stop this interference and make sure only the American people have a say in the future of our energy and federal lands policies.
sourceLabel: American Voices in Federal Lands Act on AI bots in public comments

name: Mark R. Warner
quote: Good policy starts with good data. This bipartisan legislation will finally give us a clear picture of AI's impact on the workforce – what jobs are being eliminated, which workers are being retrained, and where new opportunities are emerging.
sourceLabel: AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act announcement

name: James C. Justice
quote: A.I. chatbots are an incredible tool for older Americans, but we can't miss the opportunity to protect our seniors who rely on chatbots for support, companionship, and even important decisions during critical times. The Senior Chatbot Protection Act sets transparency standards so our seniors know they are speaking with a chatbot and not a real person.
sourceLabel: Senior Chatbot Protection Act introduction

name: Adam B. Schiff
quote: There are good reasons to use AI technology to advance our national security, however – just as with any tool, we cannot depend on technology alone to guide to us, particularly when the risks of harm can be fatal. My legislation would protect Americans from unlawful domestic surveillance, ensure that humans in the chain of command exercise responsibility for the use of any lethal technology, and maintain strong ethical protections in the deployment of autonomous and semi-autonomous weapons.
sourceLabel: HALO Act press release

name: Alex Padilla
quote: AI-powered chatbots present an unprecedented and unique danger to minors engaged in longer and unsupervised interactions with these systems. This issue is both timely and urgent, as AI is rapidly shaping how Americans – including children – learn, communicate, and seek help.
sourceLabel: FTC letter on AI chatbot risks to children

name: Christopher A. Coons
quote: Everyone deserves the right to own and protect their voice and likeness from AI deepfakes, no matter if you're Taylor Swift or an 8th grader in Wilmington. AI can be used as a tool to foster creativity, but that can't come at the expense of the unauthorized exploitation of anyone's voice or likeness.
sourceLabel: NO FAKES Act committee passage

name: Ashley Moody
quote: No one should have their voice, image, or likeness stolen and used in a fake video or AI-generated deepfake without their consent. With artificial intelligence advancing at a rapid pace, it is becoming harder for people to know what is real and what is not.
sourceLabel: NO FAKES Act committee passage

name: Rick Scott
quote: AI is opening up our economy and our daily lives to new worlds of possibility, but it's naïve to think only well-intentioned Americans are using it. We have enemies in all corners of the world, and they know how to use AI as well.
sourceLabel: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act

name: Raphael G. Warnock
quote: AI is not going anywhere. It has both promise and peril. I just want us to be thinking critically about this from all angles.
sourceLabel: Senate Banking Committee hearing on AI

name: Brian Schatz
quote: People deserve to know whether or not the videos, photos, and content they see and read online is real or not. Our bill is simple – if any content is made by artificial intelligence, it should be labeled so that people are aware and aren't fooled or scammed.
sourceLabel: AI Labeling Act

name: Joni Ernst
quote: Developing guardrails as outlined in the AI roadmap is the right thing to do, but we need to do so in a way that doesn't hinder the opportunities of the future.
sourceLabel: ARI AI Policy Impact Forum

name: Katie Boyd Britt
quote: If AI can be this brilliant, we certainly can put the proper guardrails in place to where they are not talking to our children about sexual interplay, where they are not talking to our children about illicit drug abuse, where they are not talking to our children about self-harm. This is not hard.
sourceLabel: GUARD Act introduction press conference

name: Tommy Tuberville
quote: Every day this rule remains in place, American companies face mounting uncertainty, stalled investments, and the risk of losing critical global partnerships that cannot be easily regained. Therefore, we urge you to withdraw this rule and propose an alternative that is effective in preventing Communist China from capturing the world market in a leading technology without compromising American advantages.
sourceLabel: Letter urging withdrawal of Biden AI Diffusion Rule

name: John Boozman
quote: However, while AI holds great potential, we should also ask tough questions about the potential risks. New regulations may be needed to ensure that consumers are kept safe, especially when it comes to the use of applications that handle sensitive data.
sourceLabel: Senate Agriculture hearing: AI in agriculture

name: Tom Cotton
quote: Winning the AI race will be critical to our national security and economic prosperity for decades to come. We must do everything to protect American AI dominance from adversaries like Communist China.
sourceLabel: AI dominance resolution (with Coons)

name: Mark Kelly
quote: But seniors need to know when they're talking to a machine, what its limits are, and how their information is being used to make sure they aren't being scammed or put at risk.
sourceLabel: Senior Chatbot Protection Act

name: Roger F. Wicker
quote: Any government regulations on AI must begin with a "light touch" so that innovators can experiment, prototype, and compete.
sourceLabel: Wicker column: Maintaining America's AI Edge

name: Susan M. Collins
quote: In a rapidly evolving digital landscape, we must ensure that voters are not manipulated by purposely misleading AI-generated content.
sourceLabel: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act press release

name: James E. Risch
quote: In recent years, we have had people come in here and predict what was going to happen as far as demand for electricity for America because of AI and other things that are coming on board.

notes: Editorial cites AI in cyber defense context; no direct x-risk or domestic-regulation quotes.

name: Jeanne Shaheen
quote: I am concerned that future uses of deepfake technology will be harder to detect and fend off as AI technology progresses.

notes: No x-risk or frontier-reg quotes found.

name: Martin Heinrich
quote: We each recognized the potential risks AI could present, including altering our workforce in the short-term and long term, raising questions about the application of existing laws in an AI-enabled world, changing the dynamics of our national security, and raising the threat of potential doomsday scenarios.
sourceLabel: Bipartisan Senate AI Working Group roadmap
notes: Cosponsored multiple ethics bills per actions.json; roadmap co-authored as AI Working Group co-founder.

name: Ben Ray Luján
quote: The TEST AI Act addresses these shortcomings by creating government testbeds to better evaluate AI systems. This will help leverage the talent of our National Laboratories and strengthen the federal government's ability to implement responsible guardrails that protect our national security and the American people.
sourceLabel: TEST AI Act press release
notes: Cosponsored ethics bills per actions.json.

name: Jerry Moran
quote: The Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act would require federal agencies to incorporate the NIST framework into their AI management efforts to help limit the risks that could be associated with AI technology.
sourceLabel: Federal AI Risk Management Act press release

name: Rand Paul
quote: I think a lot of these decisions will be made by the state legislature.

name: Gary C. Peters

sourceLabel: PREPARED for AI Act press release

name: Todd Young

name: Angus S. King, Jr.

sourceLabel: Extreme AI risks framework letter
notes: Cosponsored DEFIANCE Act per actions.json.

name: Steve Daines

name: Kevin Cramer

notes: Cosponsored chip-security S.1705 per actions.json.

name: Deb Fischer

notes: American COMPETE Act sponsor; no x-risk quotes found.

name: Catherine Cortez Masto
quote: I've seen firsthand how technology can drive our economy and deliver incredible innovations, but we have to make sure that there are guardrails in place to keep people safe.

name: Roger Marshall

name: Elissa Slotkin

name: Eric Schmitt

name: Angela D. Alsobrooks

name: Richard J. Durbin

name: Bill Cassidy

name: James Lankford

name: Cory A. Booker
quote: I'm glad to see that the Executive Order includes many of the principles and priorities I shared with the White House earlier this year, including the need for provisions to bolster AI research and development, promote innovation, combat AI-enabled discrimination, advance equity and civil rights, and otherwise maximize the benefits of AI for all people — not just the most fortunate.
sourceLabel: Statement on Biden AI Executive Order

name: Ted Budd
quote: As the U.S. continues our fight to maintain American leadership in AI, CAISI has also played a leading role in highlighting, in a public fashion, the relative capability of leading Chinese AI models compared to U.S. offerings.
sourceLabel: Letter to National Cyber Director on CAISI frontier-model evaluations
notes: Existing evidence covers free-market/innovation hearing quote.

name: Charles E. Schumer
quote: Each insight forum will focus on the biggest issues in AI, including… guarding against doomsday scenarios.
sourceLabel: SAFE Innovation Framework launch remarks

name: Josh Hawley
quote: It is the sense of Congress that rapidly advancing artificial intelligence capabilities present both opportunities and significant risks to national security, public safety, economic competitiveness, civil liberties, and healthy labor and other markets, and that, as artificial intelligence advances toward human-level capabilities in virtually all domains, the United States must establish a secure testing and evaluation program to generate data-driven options for managing emerging risks.
sourceLabel: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act (S.2938) — Hawley sponsor text
notes: Existing evidence includes existential-risk hearing exchange.

name: Bernie Sanders
quote: Nearly every day, there is a frightening new story about how Big Tech companies are losing control of the technology they are developing, with potentially cataclysmic results. The leaders of the major AI companies publicly acknowledge that they do not fully understand the technology and that it is escaping their control. [...] That's why I am introducing legislation to immediately pause the development of increasingly powerful AI and ban the creation of systems that humanity cannot fully control — at home and around the world. The future of humanity cannot be left in the hands of a handful of Big Tech oligarchs.
sourceLabel: Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act press release
notes: Announced forthcoming Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act with Rep. Greg Casar. No Congress.gov bill number as of 2026-09-10. Also covered by Washington Post, 2026-09-03.

name: Bernie Sanders
quote: Mr. Coxon is right. The very people building this technology admit that it could threaten the future of humanity. That is why I will soon be introducing legislation to ban superintelligence and pause AI development.
sourceLabel: X post on Jacob Coxon Anthropic resignation
notes: Public post responding to Jacob Coxon's Anthropic resignation; compiled in @daniel_271828 congressional-response thread.

name: Chris Murphy
quote: If you read anything today, read this. And remember, the problem he articulates - AI companies in a blind race to build a death machine first - can easily be solved. Through a regulatory system that allows the research to continue, but in a way that doesn't destroy us.
sourceLabel: X post on Jacob Coxon Anthropic resignation
notes: Public post responding to Jacob Coxon's Anthropic resignation; compiled in @daniel_271828 congressional-response thread.

name: Patty Murray
quote: If we are smart enough to create such powerful AI, then we are smart enough to regulate it. America can meet the moment, but the clock is ticking. Congress needs to step up and move NOW to protect American lives and safeguard our future.
sourceLabel: X post on Jacob Coxon Anthropic resignation
notes: Public post responding to Jacob Coxon's Anthropic resignation; compiled in @daniel_271828 congressional-response thread.

name: Ted Cruz
quote: AI is advancing at an extraordinary pace, and some of the risks are dangerous and frightening. I've been on the forefront of this issue in the Senate. I wrote and passed the TAKE IT DOWN Act, the only legislation Congress has enacted restricting AI [...]. We cannot stick our heads in the sand and pretend this technology isn't happening. We need guardrails. But America needs to lead.
sourceLabel: X post on Jacob Coxon Anthropic resignation
notes: Public post responding to Jacob Coxon's Anthropic resignation; compiled in @daniel_271828 congressional-response thread. Also expresses strong concern about the U.S. not coming second to China, so this x-risk signal is a bit ambiguous.

name: Chris Van Hollen
quote: Anyone still denying the risks posed by unregulated AI should read this thread. It's time to pump the brakes & take action NOW. We need: - Mandatory safeguards - A comprehensive testing regime - Urgent dialogue with China, before & during President Xi's visit to DC this month.
sourceLabel: X post on Jacob Coxon Anthropic resignation
notes: Public post amplifying Jacob Coxon's warning that labs are racing to superintelligence that could kill everyone this decade; compiled in @daniel_271828 congressional-response thread.

name: Mark Kelly
quote: AI is moving fast and we need to act now. Almost a year ago, I released AI for America because I believe we need to be proactive on AI, both harnessing its potential so it benefits working people and protecting against the worst outcomes it could lead to. The reality is that the Big Tech approach of 'build fast and break things' is not the right one for AI, and Washington needs to wake up and take this seriously.
sourceLabel: X post on Jacob Coxon Anthropic resignation
notes: Public post responding to Jacob Coxon's Anthropic resignation; compiled in @daniel_271828 congressional-response thread.

name: Ruben Gallego
quote: Most recently, an Anthropic researcher who previously worked at OpenAI resigned from the AI industry, warning about a race to develop increasingly powerful and potentially uncontrollable systems and arguing that government intervention may ultimately be necessary. [...] Leading AI researchers have warned that increasingly autonomous systems could create risks ranging from large-scale misuse to circumstances in which humans have difficulty maintaining meaningful control over advanced systems. That warning follows a broader 2023 public statement [...] declaring that mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority on par with pandemics and nuclear war.
sourceLabel: Letter urging a Senate Select Committee on AI
notes: Also posted the CAIS extinction-risk statement on X while urging an immediate bipartisan Senate Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.

name: Lisa Blunt Rochester
quote: Even if there was a 1% chance AI could wipe out human life, we should be pumping the brakes to make sure we have the proper safeguards in place, not racing blindly into disaster. It's time for Congress to step in and find the balance between safety and innovation, before it's too late.
sourceLabel: X post on Jacob Coxon Anthropic resignation
notes: Public post responding to Jacob Coxon's Anthropic resignation; compiled in @daniel_271828 congressional-response thread.
